description: Mitigate wind loads on tall buildings using aerodynamic shape tailoring: a CFD-based comparative case study is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "simulation", published or maintained by Anamika Malla, Texas Tech University (ttu.edu). The project investigates different ways of aerodynamic shape modification for mitigating wind loads on tall buildings. The target building used for this study is similar to the 432 Park Avenue building in Manhattan, New York. CFD models for five test cases with different aerodynamic shape modifications were created and monitored. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "simulation" project. Keywords: Wind loads, CFD, LES, aerodynamic shape modification, tall buildings. Published 2023-08-10. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
